motivation: In 2007 Lorimer, McLaughlin and Bailes reported a millisecond burst of radio waves in archival Parkes pulsar data. Its dispersion measure far exceeded anything the Milky Way could produce, which placed the source at cosmological distances. Many first doubted this 'Lorimer burst', but it opened an entirely new class of astrophysical transients. Thousands of FRBs have since been detected, localised to host galaxies, and linked to magnetars. FRBs now serve as precision probes of fundamental physics. Their dispersion measures have accounted for the 'missing' cosmic baryons, and they constrain the intergalactic medium, cosmic magnetism, the Hubble constant, the distance-duality relation, primordial black holes and the photon mass. The discovery came from careful, systematic searches of pulsar data, and it changed how we use the radio sky to test cosmology and gravity. It is shaping science with CHIME, MeerKAT and the coming SKA.
